item.title: Renoir 1.14.1
item.description:
Drag a new box into place, then name it when you're ready.

  • Place first, edit afterwards. Open Add Box and drag any built-in or custom stencil onto the canvas or into a container. The box stays where you drop it and is selected, with no details dialog opening automatically. You can place several boxes before editing them.
  • Choose Edit Box to enter details. Use Edit Box… in the inspector or right-click menu, or double-click the box, to give it a name, change its title font and size, and enter metadata.
  • Keep your chosen position. Editing a dropped box preserves its position, including after saving and reopening the drawing. Choose Layout whenever you want an automatic arrangement. Save Version (⌘S) keeps your additions and edits in the drawing's history.

Choose Renoir › Check for Updates… to install this version, or download the DMG, open it, and drag Renoir.app to Applications.

Requires macOS 14 or newer on Apple silicon. This installer is Developer ID signed and notarised by Apple.

item.title: Renoir 1.14.0
item.description:
Choose where your library lives, including a downloaded OneDrive folder for use across Macs one at a time.

  • Move your library from Settings. In Renoir › Settings… › General, choose Move Library… and select an empty folder. Renoir copies drawings, version history, comments, folders, custom stencils, presets, and attachments, verifies the copy, then switches to it. The original folder remains available as a recovery copy.
  • Open an existing library. Choose Open Existing Library… and select its root folder. Open Renoir windows reload the chosen library immediately, and the location is remembered on this Mac. Save drawing changes and finish open editors before switching.
  • Your AI helper follows the location. This version's MCP helper checks the current library on each request. Reconnect AI clients after updating Renoir to load the new helper.
  • Recover when a folder is unavailable. Renoir shows a Library Unavailable page with a link to Settings if a chosen folder is missing. It does not create an empty replacement at that location.

For OneDrive, mark the library folder Always Keep on This Device on each Mac and let syncing finish before switching devices.

Choose Renoir › Check for Updates… to install this version, or download the DMG, open it, and drag Renoir.app to Applications.

Requires macOS 14 or newer on Apple silicon. This installer is Developer ID signed and notarised by Apple.

item.title: Renoir 1.13.3
item.description:
Reduce repeated rendering work when moving boxes, previewing layouts, and interacting with drawings.

  • Faster layout animation. Renoir prepares relationship routes once for the destination layout and reuses them during animation. It no longer reroutes and validates the whole drawing on every animation frame.
  • Lighter canvas redraws. Stencil icons are cached after decoding, and boxes outside the visible or updated area are skipped. Unchanged scenes are reused without starting another redraw.
  • Keep larger drawings responsive. Drawings with more than 250 boxes or 80 relationships switch directly to the new layout. Animation also stops when its canvas is removed.
  • Edits stay current during movement. Title and metadata changes made during an animation are displayed immediately.

Choose Renoir › Check for Updates… to install this version, or download the DMG, open it, and drag Renoir.app to Applications.

Requires macOS 14 or newer on Apple silicon. This installer is Developer ID signed and notarised by Apple.

item.title: Renoir 1.13.2
item.description:
Reopen Renoir from the Dock and edit the heading and subtitle above your drawing.

  • Dock reopening works after closing the window. Clicking Renoir in the Dock opens its library window when the last window has been closed. A minimised window is restored without creating a second window.
  • Edit the drawing header. Choose Drawing › Edit Drawing Header…, or use the drawing inspector, to change the main heading and the smaller subtitle directly beneath it. You can also show or hide the header. Apply the changes, then choose Save Version (⌘S) to keep them in the drawing’s history. Undo and redo are supported.
  • Choose subtitle scope for diagrams with states. Apply a subtitle to the current state or every state. The heading is shared across states, and Renoir adds the state name when displaying it. The edited header appears in the canvas and exported drawings.

Choose Renoir › Check for Updates… to install this version, or download the DMG, open it, and drag Renoir.app to Applications.

Requires macOS 14 or newer on Apple silicon. This installer is Developer ID signed and notarised by Apple.

item.title: Renoir 1.13.1
item.description:
Place boxes first, enter their details afterwards, and delete boxes directly in Renoir.

  • Drop first, enter metadata second. Drag any built-in or custom stencil onto the diagram or into a container. Renoir adds the box and reruns the layout before opening its title, style, and metadata editor. Choose Later to keep the box and fill in its details afterwards. Clicking a stencil still lets you enter details before adding it.
  • Delete boxes from the UI. Select a box and press Delete, choose Drawing › Delete Box (⌘⌫), or use the inspector or right-click menu. A confirmation explains what will be removed. Deleting a container also removes its contents and attached relationships across every state. Undo and redo are available before saving.
  • Always arrange new boxes. Every insertion reruns the selected layout, including additions to empty containers and drawings without a saved layout. Diagrams with multiple states recalculate their shared slots. Drawings without a chosen layout use balanced nesting.

Choose Save Version (⌘S) to keep your box and metadata changes in the drawing’s history.

Choose Renoir › Check for Updates… to install this version, or download the DMG, open it, and drag Renoir.app to Applications.

Requires macOS 14 or newer on Apple silicon. This installer is Developer ID signed and notarised by Apple.

item.title: Renoir 1.13.0
item.description:
Create boxes from stencils and edit their titles, text style, and metadata inside Renoir.

  • Add boxes from any stencil. Add Box (⇧⌘B) opens a searchable palette of built-in and custom stencils. Drag a stencil onto the drawing or into a container, including an empty one, or click it to enter its details. The current layout makes room for new boxes; drawings without a saved layout use nesting.
  • Edit titles and metadata. Double-click a box, choose Drawing › Edit Component (⇧⌘E), or use the inspector to edit its title, description, source link, and named metadata fields. Metadata supports text, numbers, yes/no values, and structured values.
  • Choose title fonts and text sizes. Change the font family, point size, bold, and alignment, with a live preview. The canvas and PNG, PDF, SVG, and HTML exports honor the chosen title style. Layout reserves room for larger titles across diagram states.
  • Move containers with their contents. Existing boxes can be dragged into other containers. Container moves update the shared structure in every state, and Renoir prevents moves that would create a parent cycle.
  • Keep edits in history. Apply component edits to the current state or every state, undo and redo them, and use Save Version (⌘S) to keep them. Older imported drawings whose source ID differs from their library ID can now save edits correctly.

Choose Renoir › Check for Updates… to install this version, or download the DMG, open it, and drag Renoir.app to Applications.

Requires macOS 14 or newer on Apple silicon. This installer is Developer ID signed and notarised by Apple.

item.title: Renoir 1.12.0
item.description:
Edit states on the canvas, find anything in a drawing, and leave review comments.

  • Move components on the canvas. Drag a component onto another container to move it, in the state on screen for a drawing with states. Right-click for Move To, Remove from this state, Gone After, New in, and Keep in Every State. Each change previews a fresh layout for Save Version, and Edit › Undo (⌘Z) takes it back.
  • Find in the drawing. Edit › Find in Drawing (⌘F) highlights every component whose name, description, or details match and zooms to each in turn; ⌘G and ⇧⌘G step through them. Search Library is now ⌥⌘F.
  • Review comments. Comment on a component or the whole drawing from the inspector's Comments tab, by right-clicking, or with Drawing › Add Comment (⇧⌘K). Components with open comments get a marker on the canvas. Comments don't make saves and never appear in exports, and your AI client can read and resolve them with the new list_comments, add_comment, resolve_comment, and delete_comment tools.

Renoir 1.11.0 and later update themselves; choose Renoir › Check for Updates… to get this version now. From earlier versions, download the DMG, open it, and drag Renoir.app to Applications. The MCP helper is inside the app at Renoir.app/Contents/MacOS/RenoirMCP; see MCP setup for client configuration.

Requires macOS 14 or newer. Download Renoir-1.12.0-signed.dmg for the Developer ID signed and Apple notarized installer. Open the DMG and drag Renoir.app to Applications.

Automatic updates now install the signed and notarized build, including for existing Renoir 1.12.0 installations. The original Renoir-1.12.0.dmg is the earlier ad hoc build.

item.title: Renoir 1.11.0
item.description:
Renoir now keeps itself up to date.

  • Automatic updates. Renoir checks for new versions and installs them for you. Choose Renoir › Check for Updates… to check now, and turn automatic checks and installs on or off in Settings › General, which also shows the version you have.
  • Signed and checked. Updates come from Renoir's public releases at acousland/Renoir-releases, and Renoir installs one only if it's signed with Renoir's own key.
  • This is the last version to install by hand. Once you have it, later versions arrive on their own.

Download the DMG, open it, and drag Renoir.app to Applications. The MCP helper is inside the app at Renoir.app/Contents/MacOS/RenoirMCP; see MCP setup for client configuration.

Requires macOS 14 or newer. The build is ad hoc signed and has not been notarized by Apple, so macOS may ask you to approve its first launch.
